concept.description: Replace an explicit global clock or barrier with emergent phase alignment between participants.

why_interesting: The problem's 'Power and Thermal' dimension (how energy is consumed, converted and removed) is where the conventional approach carries a structural assumption: Power density is limited by heat removal, so performance is capped by thermals rather than by the logic itself. AARL took a mechanism that already works in coupled oscillator physics, chronobiology, clock distribution - Replace an explicit global clock or barrier with emergent phase alignment between participants. - and asked what happens if it is applied to Battery. If the mechanism transfers, the gain would come from removing that assumption rather than from tuning the existing design. Whether it transfers is exactly what is not established here.

failure_conditions.condition: The assumed limitation of the Power and Thermal facet does not actually hold for this system.
failure_conditions.why_it_would_break_the_direction: The direction exists to remove that limitation; if the limitation is not real, the direction has no target (this is the first assumption to check).

first_experiment.objective: Establish whether the mechanism moves energy per operation for Battery at all, before tuning anything.
first_experiment.design: Baseline A: the conventional power and thermal approach. Variant B: the Oscillator synchronization mechanism applied only to the power management dimension. Keep every other parameter identical and use the same seed/warm-up.
first_experiment.decision_rule: Only claim support if B moves energy per operation outside the run-to-run spread of A; if the spread is larger than the effect, report INCONCLUSIVE rather than a direction.
first_experiment.what_would_make_it_stop: If A is already at the physical or structural limit of energy per operation, the comparison cannot discriminate and the design must change.
